title: Adaptive microphase splitting and kernel-aware hedged routing for latency-throughput tradeoffs
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Problem: Large variance in tail latency for mixed prefill/decode workloads when kernel selection and attention-costs are misaligned across microphases. Existing phase-aware schedulers group requests by broad phases (prefill vs decode) but miss opportunities to split microphases and route short-latency-critical fragments to faster kernels or hedged paths. This leads to user-facing latency spikes for interactive use cases and suboptimal GPU utilization for throughput-oriented flows.
background: We currently use a phase-aware arbitration layer that classifies work into prefill and decode and then applies hybrid quota/priority policies. Kernel selection happens later in the execution path based on model/seq len heuristics. Recent internal experiments show that (1) attention computation cost can vary dramatically inside a single decode (long prefix + short assistant reply vs multi-turn chat), (2) some kernels (fused-attn-v2, block-sparse-attn) have lower latency for short tails but worse steady-state throughput, and (3) prefix KV cache hits create microphase boundaries that are exploitable for hedging. Customers building chat UIs are most sensitive to 95/99th tail latency while batch embedding workloads favor throughput.
goals: Reduce 95th/99th token latency for interactive chat workloads by >=20% in mixed-load clusters
Preserve or improve 50th token latency and end-to-end throughput for throughput-oriented workloads
Introduce kernel-aware microphase splitting so routing decisions can be made before heavy kernel binding
Provide clear rollout knobs and observability (per-kernel latency histograms, per-phase cost breakdown)
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end benchmark: mixed workload (60% interactive chat, 40% batch gen) shows >=20% reduction in 99th token latency on test cluster compared to baseline
No regression in average token throughput for throughput-only traces (within 5%)
Scheduler exposes two new knobs: microphase-split-threshold (ms) and hedged-routing-enabled (boolean) in runtime config
Telemetry: Console dashboards show per-kernel tail latency and fraction of requests routed to hedged fast-paths
Automated canary rollout plan exists and can be executed with runtime flag toggles
design_decision_log: 2026-03-01: Proposal to split phases at microphase boundaries (KV cache transitions, attention window changes) accepted by runtime team
2026-03-03: Decided against always using fused-attn-v2 for short tails — leads to throughput cliffs under contention; instead use hedged routing with fallback
2026-03-05: Opted to add a lightweight kernel-cost estimator in prefill stage to predict per-request kernel latency distribution rather than relying solely on sequence-length heuristics
2026-03-08: Chosen metrics: 95th/99th token latency, core-hours per 1M tokens, kernel-bound contention ratio
implementation_plan: Phase A (spike): implement microphase detector in prefill path that emits candidate split points (prefill end, KV cache fill levels, attention-window-change) - 2d
Phase B: add kernel-cost estimator that ingests model metadata + microphase hint + current HW utilization -> cost bucket - 3d
Phase C: implement hedged-routing: short-path route to low-latency kernel with timeout Xms and automatic fallback to throughput kernel - 5d
Phase D: telemetry plumbing and console dashboards for per-kernel KPIs - 3d
Phase E: integration tests, load tests, and canary rollout automation - 4d
testing_plan: Create mixed synthetic traces derived from Prod Chat traces (obfuscated) and embeddings traces. Run cluster-level A/B tests with toggle lymph (canary) using a 5% traffic slice. Validate correctness: ensure token order/consistency, no KV corruption. Add microbench harness for kernel estimator accuracy (predicted vs observed latency distributions).
metrics: 99th token latency (ms) per model per region
Fraction of requests taking hedged fast-path
Kernel fallback rate and fallback latency delta
rollout_plan: Start with internal cluster (non-customer) with hedged-routing disabled by default: enable telemetry only
Stage 1: enable microphase detection + kernel cost estimator with hedged-routing off; collect signals for 48h
Stage 2: enable hedged-routing for 2 internal services (search-chat, demo app) at 5% of traffic for 24h
Stage 3: expand to 20% with automated rollback if 99th latency worsens by >5% or core-hours increases by >10%
Stage 4: full rollout after 7 days of stable metrics and SRE signoff
risks_mitigation: Risk: Hedged fast-path may double GPU kernel launches and increase core-hours. Mitigation: dynamic hedging: only enable for requests predicted to yield >=Xms savings; circuit-breaker when core-hour delta exceeds threshold

Risk: Mis-prediction sends long requests to low-throughput kernel causing queue buildup. Mitigation: add short admission check at kernel bind time (reject hedged route if current kernel queue > threshold)
Risk: Observability blind spots. Mitigation: tag traces with kernel-id, microphase-id, and route decision to enable postmortem analysis
open_questions: What is the optimal threshold for microphase splitting (ms) that balances added scheduling overhead vs latency benefit?
Should hedging be rate-limited per-GPU or per-cluster?
How do we incorporate quantized-kernel performance profiles (int8 vs fp16) into cost estimator without exploding feature space?
Do we need a graceful degradation policy for very-high contention events (global capacity alarms)?
notes: This ticket intentionally focuses on routing and scheduling decisions prior to final kernel binding. Subsequent follow-ups should address kernel-level micro-optimizations (fusion tuning) and cross-model QoS policies. Coordinate with SRE for canary thresholds and billing team for core-hour accounting.
